clue.text: None left? O.K.

definitions.meaning: if every one remains, the whole lot is still there, with nothing departed

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: with all of them still in place, none has left.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'every one is present' and the everyday 'fine, acceptable'.

clue.text: Poet or libertine with a taste for fine fabric

parts.note: someone with a taste for a thing loves it
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A dandyish poet or rake who adores luxurious cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Lovelace was a Cavalier poet; Lovelace is also the rake who pursues the heroine in Richardson's novel Clarissa.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the 17th-century Cavalier versifier and to the seducer in Clarissa.

clue.text: BR's revolutionary investment ?

parts.note: British Rail's capital tied up in wheeled carriages and wagons; a stock is an investment and wheels revolve

explanation.surface: British Rail putting money into something radical.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the old UK state railway. 'Revolutionary' sounds political but means turning on wheels, and 'investment' is a stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages and wagons are the fleet a railway owns, and their wheels go round.

clue.text: Scandalous behaviour of departing heir

parts.note: going means leaving
a son is the classic heir

explanation.surface: The disgraceful conduct of an heir who is leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or shady carryings-on are called by this idiom.

clue.text: Bad tennis with no score produces strain

indicators.note: bad here signals the letters of the word are played badly, rearranged

parts.note: a score of nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Poor tennis played without a point on the board makes for stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' reshuffles TENNIS together with O (zero, no score) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautness or stress is a synonym of strain.

clue.text: The answer about civil wrong-doing

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a tort is a wrong in civil law

explanation.surface: A reply concerning a breach of civil law.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp reply or riposte is a synonym.

clue.text: One party returns to the island

indicators.note: returns means these pieces come back, read from right to left

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Lab is the short form of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political party comes back to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns I and LAB around together, giving BAL followed by I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island east of Java is the place meant.

clue.text: Astounds deer-hunters ?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., those who go after stags

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means amazes, and split up it suggests people who pursue male deer.

clue.text: Great transpontine beast at the crossroads

definitions.text: Great transpontine beast at the crossroads

parts.words: Great transpontine beast at the crossroads
parts.note: a huge animal, and also the name of a busy road junction south of the Thames, across the bridges from central London

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transpontine' means across the bridge: Elephant and Castle is a famous road junction in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest land animal also names the south London junction Elephant and Castle.

clue.text: A bit of a squash for all-round cricketers here ?

definitions.text: A bit of a squash for all-round cricketers here ?

parts.words: A bit of a squash for all-round cricketers here ?
parts.note: a shape that is a slightly squashed circle, and a London cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a Test cricket ground in south London; the shape is a round that has been a bit squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: An elongated, flattened circle is this shape, which is also the name of a famous cricket venue.

clue.text: Boasting about achieving an enfilade

definitions.meaning: an enfilade is gunfire raking along a line of troops from end to end

explanation.definitionFit: The slang term for bragging, read literally, means firing along a rank of soldiers.

clue.text: Moving picture with impressionistic technique

definitions.meaning: shifting from one place to another
making a picture by pressing a transfer design onto a surface, an impression technique

explanation.definitionFit: The word means relocating, and also making images by pressing decals onto a surface.

clue.text: Favourite spots where the ghost walks

explanation.definitionFit: Favourite places one frequents, and the places a spectre is said to visit.

clue.text: Alfresco cooking installation to have wider scope?

parts.note: alfresco means out of doors, outside
a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: An outdoor barbecue set-up that reaches further.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach further than something is to exceed its reach, a verb of extent.

clue.text: Quarters for sailor boys ?

parts.note: sea suggests a sailor's world, used here as a seafaring prefix
sons are boys

explanation.surface: Lodgings for young lads in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like living space aboard ship; it means the four parts of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring, summer, autumn and winter each make up a quarter of the year.

clue.text: Reducing weight of thin porcelain

parts.note: slim means thin
Ming is Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Lightening the load of delicate china.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieting to lose pounds is the sense.

clue.text: Pots, with directions included, of old health-drinks

indicators.note: included means one piece is placed inside the word pots

parts.note: S, S and E are compass directions south, south, east

explanation.surface: Jars packed with instructions for old-fashioned tonics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' looks like instructions on the jar; it gives compass points SSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot milk curdled with ale or wine was an old remedy drink.

clue.text: Upset about music-hall act

parts.note: over can mean about, as in 'argue over'
a turn is a performer's act in variety

explanation.definitionFit: To knock over or capsize is a synonym.

clue.text: Dribbled for a spell and went ahead

parts.note: a trick can be a stint or turn, a spell of duty
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A footballer ran with the ball for a while and took the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: A trick is a shift at the helm or on watch, a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowed in a thin stream is a synonym for dribbled.

clue.text: Straight flyer gets medal again, something to prize

parts.note: a crow, as in 'as the crow flies'
a bar on a medal ribbon marks the same award earned a second time

explanation.surface: A direct bird wins another decoration, a thing to treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' means to lever open, not to value.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever for prising things open is the tool meant.

clue.text: Tax — in the alternative, fraud

parts.note: an impost is a tax or duty
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A tax, or else a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender or fake person is a fraud.

clue.text: Not his sort, being in the fashion

indicators.note: sort means the letters of these words are sorted into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: The old word means stylish, fashionable.

clue.text: Female adviser, I agree, is crazy

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of the phrase are jumbled madly

explanation.surface: A woman counsellor admits she is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges IAGREE. Egeria was the nymph who advised King Numa of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the nymph who counselled Numa is used for any woman mentor.

clue.text: What the cowman does to his herd. How feeble:

definitions.text: What the cowman does to his herd
definitions.meaning: a dairyman draws off milk and gives the cattle drink

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a dairy farmer's daily chores and also means insipid or weak.

clue.text: Bird with strings attached

definitions.meaning: a stringed instrument of ancient Greece

explanation.definitionFit: A harp-like stringed instrument also names an Australian songbird with a showy tail.

clue.text: Man hears bride's answer shortly

indicators.note: hears means we take the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a bride answers 'I will', shortened to I'll

explanation.surface: A husband listens to his wife's wedding vow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is an example of an island.

clue.text: Liquid gas source

parts.note: a body of water that is also the source of Britain's natural gas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' suggests liquefied gas; it means watery: the North Sea supplies Britain's natural gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of water east of Britain yields much of the country's natural gas.

clue.text: Good Provencal king, sadly aged, becomes turncoat

parts.note: Good King Rene ruled Provence in the 15th century

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of aged are messed up

explanation.surface: A kindly old southern French monarch grows old and changes sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter or traitor is one who switches allegiance.
